summary: Bad Work-Life Balance
pros: They have a reputation for getting work, so they do hire.
cons:
Bad work life balance. I'd worked with IPC before the pandemic. I told myself I wouldn't be back after my stint with them pre-pandemic, but they were the only place hiring in 2024 so I had to come back. Unfortunately, the company's attitude towards their freelancers has declined since then. IPC is known for their content and they do produce great tv shows, but they do it at the expense of their employees. Their first big show was Emmy-nominated and critically beloved, but it came at the expense of the staff on the show. The host of the show was particularly cruel to the staff and for a long time, IPC turned a blind eye to her treatment of staff because the show was so big.

I've come back now and that show is now gone. The outright cruelty isn't there, but the disregard for the staff is still present. Unfortunately, the industry seems to be shifting towards a pattern of creating high content with low budgets. IPC has gladly embraced that and is inking deals with low budgets while still expecting crew to pick up the slack. Productions have very little budget and reduced support on set while still expected to delivery high-quality content. Post works extremely long hours to try to pick up the slack and IPC is more than happy that people work from home now so they can "keep working". Requests for more help are ignored until the problems are too big and teams are scrambling to catch up.

If you can hang with this, they do hire and seem to re-hire people they like working with. Or, most accurately, re-hire people they know will work their crazy schedules. If you're planning on taking a job with them, be clear about your availability and the schedule they're requesting.
advice: Care about your people. Reduce your overhead if you need to rather than reducing the help needed on your projects. CARE ABOUT YOUR PEOPLE.

summary: Fun work environment, but you'll feel burned out every shift.
pros:
My coworkers are kind and honest. The work is fun when it can be and some of the customers have a good spirit. When it comes to your break, you can at least afford your snacks/meals cause they're cheap. I find it fun to look into what my customers are buying. Managers are great and modest about their greatness. 
Would recommend to a friend because there are worser places to work at.
cons:
Some people have been consistently calling out in my area and I am burnt out from people who don't show up when they're scheduled to. 
If you're a cashier, you only get a ten minute break and it's not enough time for ramen. You'll feel lucky when you get 30 minutes for covering someone else's shift. 
Corporate is dramatic with some of their rules, like it's considered theft if you don't pay for your food, but you require a manager to be present in order to pay for it, and managers can be busy at times. Some customers can be quite impatient whilst making the line longer with demands, especially if they don't calculate their finances whilst shopping. 
Some of the technology is old and when it's broken down, I am told that I am not allowed to put "out of order" signs up.
Some customers don't understand that they should never pay with a $100 bill early in the morning at any store.
If you want to volunteer and do extra work without a payroll, you will be told that you can get written up for it because they have to pay you. 
The trainings on workday are obvious that they're old by many years and have not been updated to match new policies.
